name: Weekly Paclitaxel (single-agent) for Angiosarcoma
cyclesNote: continue to progression or unacceptable toxicity; angiosarcoma is uniquely taxane-sensitive. Physician determines duration.

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Soft Tissue Sarcoma (general reference)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Weekly paclitaxel is a histology-directed cytotoxic option; angiosarcoma is distinctively taxane-sensitive. Not molecularly biomarker-restricted.

premedications.name: Hypersensitivity prophylaxis
premedications.notes: corticosteroid (e.g. dexamethasone), an H1 antihistamine, and an H2 blocker before paclitaxel to reduce infusion-reaction risk from the solvent vehicle. Weekly schedules often use a reduced steroid pre-med after the first tolerated doses, physician determined.

supportiveCare: monitor for infusion / hypersensitivity reactions during the first minutes of each infusion.
peripheral sensory neuropathy is cumulative; assess before each dose and hold or reduce for grade 2 to 3.
CBC before each weekly dose; hold for significant neutropenia or thrombocytopenia.

doseModificationRules.text: Hold until improvement then resume at a reduced dose; discontinue for persistent grade 3. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Paclitaxel
drugs.notes: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 IV over about 1 hour on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle (weekly, single-agent), a standard weekly schedule used in taxane-sensitive angiosarcoma. Give hypersensitivity pre-medication. Dose per the engine from patient BSA. Standard weekly dosing, general reference (NCCN / DeVita); own wording, DRAFT.

provenance.locator: weekly single-agent paclitaxel for angiosarcoma (standard schedule)
